ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) consolidated list, OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions registries under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and the Quebec anti-corruption register, in addition to domestic and FATF-compliant politically exposed person (PEP) due diligence; each natural person must undergo continuous monitoring; adverse hits must be escalated to legal counsel and FINTRAC where applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Name Approval and Enterprise Register (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, a Quebec limited partnership's registered name must be in French; the legal designation must be 'société en commandite' or abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; an English or other-language version may be used only if a French version is also registered with equal or greater prominence; transliteration to Latin alphabetic characters with correct French accents is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises refuses the proposed name, the applicant may file a written application for administrative review ('demande de révision') within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching the original decision, corrected French name options, and, where applicable, the ministerial authorization or competent body consent for sensitive tokens; the registrar must remit its review decision; an adverse review decision may then be challenged before the competent Quebec court in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, respecting the applicable limitation periods.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally acceptable for a Quebec limited partnership engaged in an EMR/HealthTech software business, provided the partnership maintains a physical establishment address in Quebec where statutory records may be inspected and legal process can be served; the address cannot be a mere post-office box and must correspond to a genuine workplace or commercial service provider; given the SaaS nature, no clinical premises are required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 8% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registraire des entreprises or Revenu Québec, increasing to 15% if the partnership claims Quebec tax incentives, has a high volume of cross-border transactions with related non-resident partners, or is selected for a FATF-oriented Canada Revenue Agency or FINTRAC review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2200-2234 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 2, 9-32 (registration and disclosure); regulations thereunder, including the Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Quebec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Initial Registration Statement) of a Limited Partnership, filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; capital contributions are set by the limited partnership agreement. No escrow account is imposed by the Civil Code of Québec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises for SaaS/EMR limited partnerships.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation and registration of the limited partnership under the Civil Code of Québec be ratified. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the limited partnership agreement, as presented, is approved and adopted, including the admission of the general and limited partners and their respective capital contributions. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the partnership be established at [address], Quebec. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the general partner appoints [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer. FURTHER RESOLVED, that such officers and counsel are authorized to file the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, open bank accounts, and take all ancillary actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners in private execution; subsequently registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) through the initial registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement in accordance with Civil Code of Québec arts. 2200-2234. The agreement must identify at least one general partner who is liable without limitation and at least one limited partner whose liability is limited to their contribution. Define the partnership name, principal establishment, objects, contributions, profit-sharing, management powers, transfer restrictions, and dissolution provisions. Execution must occur in writing, signed by all partners or their attorneys. Notarization is not mandatory for a purely movable-services partnership, but authentication may be required if the partnership acquires immovable property. After execution, retain the original and provide a certified copy to counsel for filing.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement executed by all general and limited partners
Capital contribution schedule and acknowledgments
Resolution of the general partner authorizing registration, if the general partner is a corporation
Identification documents for individuals and certified constitutive documents for corporate partners
Power of attorney if a representative executes on behalf of any partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner challenges the agreement or refuses execution, obtain a declaration of intention and mediate; alternatively redraft the agreement and secure new signatures. If an executing representative lacks authority, cure by procuring a retroactive power of attorney or a ratifying board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete name search and reservation with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online name search and reservation system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search using the REQ's enterprise name search tool to confirm the desired name is not confusingly similar to an existing name or trademark. The name of a limited partnership must include the words 'limited partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.' or 's.e.n.c.' for a general partnership but for a limited partnership use 'limited partnership' or 'LP' as permitted by the REQ. File an online name reservation application with the REQ; a reservation is valid for 90 days. If the name is refused, the registrar will issue reasons; the applicant may amend the name or file a reply.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form (online or prescribed form)
Name search report printed from the REQ's database
Written explanation of distinctiveness and proposed use, if requested
Trademark search certificate if relying on a registered trademark as the distinctive component
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or objected to, submit a rebuttal memorandum addressing the registrar's confusion analysis, offer a revised name, or petition for administrative review. If the refusal persists, seek judicial review before the Court of Québec (Civil Division).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the initial registration declaration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online filing service at www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca or counter service at a REQ office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the initial registration declaration for a limited partnership through the REQ online portal. The declaration must state the partnership name, principal establishment address in Quebec, the general partner's full name and domicile, the object of the partnership (development and provision of electronic medical record (EMR) clinical workflow software as a service), and, if applicable, the enterprise number of the general partner if it is already registered. Attach any required schedules, and pay the registration fee by integrated payment. The REQ will assign the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and issue an attestation of registration.
required_dossiers: Initial Registration Statement (Déclaration d'immatriculation) duly signed by an authorized partner or attorney
Limited partnership agreement or an extract containing required registered information
Proof of name reservation, if applicable
Proof of principal establishment address in Quebec (e.g., lease or deed of ownership)
Certificate of attestation or constitutive documents for corporate general partner
Payment receipt for filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ sends a notice of irregularity or requests additional information, file a corrective declaration within the prescribed delay. If the application is refused, submit a formal request to the REQ requesting administrative review with supporting evidence; a subsequent refusal may be appealed to the Court of Québec within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register tax accounts with Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec - Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ integration) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ assigned by the REQ, complete the centralized business registration with Revenu Québec immediately after immatriculation. The online portal will synchronize registration for provincial accounts: GST/HST, QST, source deductions for employees, and the health services fund, if applicable. Separately, the partnership must obtain a CRA business number and register for the federal GST/HST account, a payroll deductions account, and any import/export program numbers if relevant. Confirm that the partnership's fiscal year-end is selected, usually December 31, and that returns will be filed by each partner for their share of partnership income. For a U.S. or foreign general partner, entities must confirm tax residency documentation and treaty eligibility.
required_dossiers: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) attestation from REQ
Partnership agreement and principal establishment details
Identification documents of all partners and, for corporate partners, certificate of incorporation and proof of director or officer authority
CRA Business Number confirmation or application reference
GST/HST and QST registration questionnaire responses
Payroll program registration data if employees will be hired
U.S. or other foreign tax residency certificates and W-8 and/or equivalent forms, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec or the CRA rejects or queries a registration, respond via the applicable online portal with corrected information or missing schedules. For erroneous registrations, an objection can be filed within 90 days of the notice; alternatively, the partnership may withdraw and reapply with the corrected data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt and maintain partnership governance records and minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner(s) and partners in accordance with the limited partnership agreement; annual declaration filings with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) are required by law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the partnership minute book containing the limited partnership agreement, the initial registration declaration, certificates of registration, partner register, capital account ledgers, and written resolutions of the general partner. Adopt a written resolution approving the registered office address, banking mandates, any initial officers or attorneys-in-fact, and the execution of customer and vendor agreements. Endeavor to continue with all REQ annual updates thereafter; the REQ requires the filing of an annual declaration for every registered enterprise, including limited partnerships, within the statutorily prescribed delay after each anniversary.
required_dossiers: Original limited partnership agreement
Initial registration declaration and REQ attestation
Register of partners showing capital contributions and percentage interests
Written resolutions of the general partner appointing officers and establishing banking authorities
Banking authorizations and e-signature mandate forms
Blank share/interest transfer ledger pages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If no annual declaration is filed, the REQ may issue a notice of default and the partnership may be struck from the register. Cure by filing the overdue annual declaration and paying the applicable late fee, and apply for restoration of registration if struck; judicial restoration may be sought if the registrar refuses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit a preliminary privacy and health-information governance clearance through the CAI framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI) and, if applicable, Health Canada's Medical Devices Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an EMR SaaS platform serving Quebec medical clinics, comply with the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, CQLR c P-39.1. Designate a person responsible for privacy protection, implement a privacy governance program and a privacy impact assessment (PIA) for the EMR software, and document the data flows involving medical records. If the software meets the definition of a 'medical device' under the Food and Drugs Act and its Regulations, a medical device licence may be required from Health Canada; a formal classification analysis should be retained to determine whether the product is a Class I, II, or higher, and to confirm whether a licence is necessary. For software merely processing EMR data without making diagnostic or treatment decisions, Health Canada licensing may not be triggered, but this determination should be documented in the compliance file. File any mandatory breach reports to the CAI under the private-sector privacy law whenever confidentiality incidents occur.
required_dossiers: Privacy governance program and designation of privacy officer
Privacy impact assessment (PIA) for the EMR platform
Inventory of personal health information and data flows
Health Canada medical device classification analysis or licence, if triggered
Incident response and breach management policy
Standard data processing agreements with clinics, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CAI or Health Canada issues an inquiry, respond by submitting the requested documentation and a compliance plan; if an adverse classification is issued from Health Canada, request an advisory opinion or file a reclassification application. If a privacy breach notification obligation is disputed, preserve a detailed incident file and, if necessary, seek an exemption or ruling from the CAI.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for registration and legal publicity; Health Canada - Medical Devices Directorate for software as a medical device classification or licence; Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI) for personal health information privacy oversight; Revenu Québec and municipal authorities for physical occupancy and tax registration; Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) for building and fire safety matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Attestation d'immatriculation d'entreprise (Enterprise Registration Attestation) issued by the REQ; Health Canada Medical Device Licence, where applicable; and municipal occupancy permit for any physical office or server-room premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Direction des évaluations environnementales
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for a SaaS software operation unless the principal establishment includes a physical data-centre or a high-energy infrastructure project triggering review under the Environmental Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2. Typical office leaseholds are not subject to an environmental impact assessment; a simple municipal use and occupancy authorization is sufficient.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The principal establishment, if containing an on-premise server room, must comply with municipal stormwater and wastewater discharge bylaws; the Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 4.1) governs any emergency backup generator emissions; ozone-depleting substances must be kept contained. Waste electrical and electronic equipment must be managed through a permitted recycler under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises. For general office activity, no liquid industrial discharge is authorized to waterways; all effluents must be discharged to the municipal sewer system under the municipal sewer use bylaw, and any chemical waste from battery backup systems is governed by the Regulation respecting hazardous materials and the Environmental Quality Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards_note: The schema's 'discharge_and_emissions_standards' field is included as a string.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The partnership must obtain a municipal occupancy permit for the physical office or server-room premises. Workplace fire safety clearance under the Fire Safety Act (CQLR c S-3.4) and the Quebec Building Code is required, including smoke alarms, emergency exits, extinguishers, and evacuation plans verified by the local fire department or preferred by a certified fire-safety inspector. If the establishment provides any server room with raised floors or heavy infrastructure, a structural load inspection by an engineer licensed in Quebec and, where applicable, an RBQ permit or certification is required. Occupational health and safety clearance is obtained by registering with the CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) and just reaching compliance with the Act respecting occupational health and safety, CQLR c S-2.1, including electrical safety, ergonomics, first-aid kits, and an evacuation warden arrangement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal GST/HST and income tax administration; Revenu Québec — Quebec provincial income tax, QST, and payroll administration. Portals: CRA Business Registration Online and My Business Account; Revenu Québec Mon dossier entreprise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited partnership must first determine whether it is carrying on business in Canada/Quebec. If required to register, obtain a federal Business Number (BN) through the CRA’s Business Registration Online, or by filing Form RC1. For Quebec, register with Revenu Québec for a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and a QST account, typically using the BN. Non-resident applicants must provide the partnership agreement, home-jurisdiction registration evidence, and identification of all partners. Quebec law may require designation of an attorney for service of process. After approval, the partnership receives its BN/QST account and must file periodic GST/HST and QST returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general check-the-box entity classification election. A Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax and is treated separately as a person for GST/HST and QST. Procedural elections available include simplified accounting methods for GST/HST, such as the Quick Method, and certain elections under the Excise Tax Act respecting input tax credit allocation. Hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory and non-elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD annual worldwide taxable supply threshold for GST/HST small supplier status; $30,000 CAD equivalent threshold for QST. Non-residents carrying on a commercial activity in Quebec or supplying digital services in Canada may be required to register regardless of this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time transaction clearance or digital stamping regime exists for ordinary B2B supplies in Canada or Quebec. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and Peppol standards are permitted. Registered suppliers must issue invoices containing prescribed GST/HST and QST information and retain electronic records for at least six years. Tax filings and remittances are submitted through CRA and Revenu Québec online systems and APIs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for zero-rating when exported from Canada and evidence shows delivery outside Canada. Services, including EMR SaaS and cloud software, supplied to a non-resident are generally zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act unless the service relates to Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada or is otherwise excluded. QST zero-rating follows analogous export principles. The supplier must be registered and must retain evidentiary documents demonstrating the non-resident recipient and actual delivery or use outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency B13 Export Declaration (for physical goods; generally not applicable to pure SaaS services)
Customs or commercial invoice identifying the non-resident purchaser
Bill of lading or alternate evidence of export delivery where goods are bundled with services
Master Subscription Agreement / SOW for the EMR SaaS platform
Non-resident status evidence such as foreign registration certificate or registered office address
Service delivery logs, server records, IP addresses, or remote access evidence proving use outside Canada
Bank remittance or inward payment records confirming receipt of cross-border consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating and reassess GST/HST and QST at 14.975% where export substantiation is inadequate. Interest is compounded daily. Under the Excise Tax Act, knowingly or grossly negligently making a false or omitted statement can attract a penalty of 25% of the tax amount involved, plus additional administrative penalties. Reassessment periods extend indefinitely where misrepresentation, negligence, or fraud is established. Criminal prosecution can result in fines and imprisonment. QST penalties under Quebec tax administration law are similarly severe.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the sole issuing and monetary authority, acting as fiscal agent and manager of Canada's official international reserves. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration; prudential oversight of banks rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while transaction-level cross-border surveillance is administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. The Minister of Finance holds formal control of the Exchange Fund Account, but no exchange-control statute restricts currency movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an unconditional IMF Article VIII jurisdiction: both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible, and the Canadian dollar is free-floating with no official convertibility ceiling, no prior-approval regime, and no repatriation or licensing hurdles for non-resident capital. For this Quebec Limited Partnership, the only practical convertibility frictions are: (i) Part XIII/Quebec withholding tax at source on distributions to non-resident partners (mitigated by tax treaties and by structuring distributions as loan repayments or guaranteed payments where commercially defensible); (ii) Canadian bank KYC/AML friction on inbound contribution wires, particularly where the remitter is a non-resident partner; and (iii) documentation of the LP's functional currency for IFRS/CTA purposes under CRA administrative practice. There are no exchange-control surrender or licensing requirements affecting the SaaS revenue stream.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for surrender, deposit, repatriation, or mandatory conversion of export receipts. EMR SaaS subscription proceeds invoiced in USD or CAD by the Quebec LP may be held indefinitely in foreign-currency accounts at Schedule I banks, swept offshore, or converted through any registered Canadian dealer without CRA or Bank of Canada approval. The only binding duties are (i) accurate trade-in-services reporting under Statistics Canada's survey framework; (ii) FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer (EFT) reporting by the financial intermediary for transactions at or above C$10,000; and (iii) the LP's obligation to furnish source-of-funds documentation to its clearing bank to avoid anomalous-activity flags on recurring USD inflows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account (CAD/USD multi-currency) plus Capital Escrow Account for LP subscription contributions
Operational Account (CAD/USD) with dedicated USD clearing and SWIFT GPI outbound capability
Operating Account and USD concentration account using BMO Harris correspondent rails for same-day USD clearing
Operational Account and FX-forward counterparty account for USD/CAD hedging trades

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an ancillary rail; Low as a primary treasury repository. Canada does not recognize the EU/UK EMI licence category; a foreign electronic money institution may only operate in Canada as a registered money services business (MSB) under the PCMLTFA, with mandatory FINTRAC registration, and it may not take deposits or extend credit without a Canadian bank charter. Wise Business, Payoneer, and similar providers are viable for low-value payroll and contractor disbursements and for multi-currency receive accounts, but they lack: (i) CDIC deposit insurance, (ii) direct access to Lynx (Canada's high-value RTGS), and (iii) relationship stability for an LP holding capital contributions. Stripe Billing is retained as the merchant acquiring rail for clinic credit/debit card payments, settling in CAD to the National Bank operating account, while all treasury liquidity and committed capital remain in Schedule I bank accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in-person or high-definition video-KYC interview for at least one authorized signatory of the General Partner. Quebec tier-1 banks will not open a fully remote account for a newly formed Limited Partnership with non-resident limited partners; the standard protocol requires: (i) physical attendance at a Montreal branch (or a verified affiliate branch abroad, e.g., RBC Royal Bank or BMO Harris) by the General Partner's signing officer; (ii) board/GP resolutions certifying signatory authority; (iii) certified true copies of the Quebec declaration of registration (Registraire des entreprises du Québec) and the LP agreement; and (iv) notarized KYC packages for each limited partner holding 25% or more, with identity verified by a Canadian consulate or a correspondent bank if the partner cannot attend personally. Video-KYC is acceptable only where the signatory already maintains a qualifying relationship with the same banking group or where the account is exclusively a settlement account for a licensed payment processor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity of the LP structure: undisclosed limited partners, nominee holdings, or broad General Partner discretion preventing the bank from completing the 'ultimate beneficial owner at or above 25%' identification test.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed LP agreement with an attached UBO schedule; current Registraire des entreprises du Québec attestation; partner registry extract; signed UBO declarations from every limited partner; organizational chart countersigned by the General Partner; Quebec certificate of good standing; legal opinion confirming no bearer or nominee interests exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners (permitted by the structure) resident in foreign jurisdictions triggering enhanced due diligence, Politically Exposed Person (PEP) screening flags, or source-of-funds suspicion on inbound capital wires.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificates for each non-resident partner; OECD Common Reporting Standard self-certification (CRA Form RC518); FATCA Forms W-8BEN-E or W-9 as applicable; PEP status declarations; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; bank reference letters from the partners' remitting institutions; a written economic-nexus narrative describing the partners' commercial rationale for the Quebec EMR venture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory/privacy underwriting concern: the EMR health-data business triggers Quebec Law 25 and PIPEDA obligations, and the bank's technology-vertical due diligence may question whether the SaaS licence status is clean and whether clinic PHI flows create operational or reputational risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) aligned with Quebec Law 25; PIPEDA compliance certificate; SOC 2 Type II report; ISO 27001 certificate; executed data-processing agreements with each medical clinic customer; legal opinion confirming that pure B2B EMR software does not constitute a regulated 'health information network' or Quebec professional-order activity; HIPAA alignment attestation for any US-derived data; cyber-liability insurance certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-monitoring mismatch between declared business scope (ISIC 6201 software licensing) and recurring payment descriptors, causing Stripe Billing settlement deposits or subscription invoices to be misclassified as medical-consultation fees and generating alerts on the operating account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardized SaaS master subscription agreement; published price list; invoice templates with unambiguous 'software licence and technical support' language; federal GST and Quebec QST registration confirmation; FINTRAC cross-border EFT reports where applicable; monthly reconciliation statements mapping Stripe payout batches to bank account credits; a standing monitoring narrative provided to the bank's financial intelligence unit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound protocol for non-resident LP capital contributions: (1) remitter executes a SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPT' (capital payment) or 'EQUI' (equity investment contribution), designating the Quebec LP's name, the National Bank/RBC account number, and institution/transit codes in field 57D, with field 70 reading 'LP capital contribution'; (2) USD wires clear through the bank's US correspondent (e.g., BMO Harris or RBC's New York branch) while CAD wires achieve same-day finality through Lynx, Canada's SWIFT-enabled high-value RTGS; (3) the first contribution must be pre-announced to the bank's trade-surveillance desk to prevent an automatic compliance hold; (4) the LP delivers on demand the executed subscription agreement, partner identification, and source-of-funds bank statements; (5) FINTRAC cross-border EFT reporting applies at or above C$10,000 per transaction, with the LP obligated to provide accurate remitter/beneficiary particulars; (6) funds remain uninvested in the Capital Escrow Account until post-receipt compliance review is completed and the bank confirms the capital can be deployed to operating or escrow accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EMR SaaS operating outflows (cloud infrastructure, licensing, subcontractors, international payroll): (a) domestic CAD supplier payments use Lynx via the bank's host-to-host channel, providing irrevocable real-time finality; (b) USD and cross-border disbursements use SWIFT MT103 over SWIFT GPI with purpose code 'SUPP' (supplier payment) or 'ROYA' (royalty/licence), embedding invoice references in field 72 to satisfy the beneficiary bank's AML screening; (c) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) are reserved exclusively for large hardware/escrow purchases where documentary conformity is required against a master purchase agreement; (d) multi-currency concentration accounts at National Bank/BMO enable zero-balancing sweeps across USD, CAD, and EUR ledger positions; (e) recurring subscription payments to foreign vendors are executed through ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.008 mandates submitted electronically, eliminating manual wire risk; (f) Stripe Billing remains the customer-facing merchant rail, with daily ACH/EFT settlement batches flowing into the CAD operating account and reconciled against invoiced clinic subscriptions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD) documented under a Canadian Master Agreement or ISDA 2002 with a Schedule I bank counterparty
FX swaps (simultaneous spot/forward principal exchange) for managing USD subscription inflow mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for hedging USD-denominated debt or capital expenditure exposure
Plain-vanilla OTC FX options on USD/CAD for asymmetric protection of the revenue base
CME-listed USD/CAD futures for exchange-traded, margin-efficient hedging of short-term receivable exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited strictly to currencies with legal convertibility restrictions (e.g., emerging-market clinic vendor currencies) where deliverability is impossible; NDFs are not required for CAD/USD, which trades as a fully deliverable pair

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) of the Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the month following the anniversary month of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of $50 CAD per year; continued default may result in administrative strike-off of the enterprise registration and loss of legal capacity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for limited partnerships under Quebec law unless mandated by the partnership agreement, a lender, or a governmental funding compact; otherwise voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) per CPA Canada; partnership records must be maintained to permit preparation of accurate tax information slips.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration must confirm and update beneficial ownership information, including any individual who directly or indirectly holds a significant interest (≥25% participation or voting rights) in the partnership, as required under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (partnership is fiscally transparent; profits are taxed in the hands of partners)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level corporate tax rate applies to the Limited Partnership. Eligible corporate general partner may access the Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction, producing a combined federal-Québec rate of 12.2% on eligible active business income up to $500,000; the combined general corporate rate is 26.5%. Federal and Québec SR&ED refundable investment tax credits are available for qualifying EMR software development expenditures.
